q: Earnings transactions of the Railways which cannot immediately be finally adjusted, including those awaiting apportionment among the railways concerned, are held pending final adjustment under the suspense head:

options.A: Traffic Suspense
options.C: PAO Suspense
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense

e: Earnings that cannot be finally adjusted at once, including amounts awaiting apportionment among the railways concerned, are held under Traffic Suspense, the suspense head for earnings transactions pending final adjustment.

q: In the investment (Plan Head) classification of the Railways, Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) are classified under Plan Head:
e: In the Plan Head classification, 71 is Stores Suspense and 72 is Manufacturing Suspense, while Miscellaneous Advances (Capital) carry Plan Head 73.

q: In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, the variations between the Final Grant and the actual expenditure under each head are dealt with by:

options.A: Ignoring the variations altogether
options.B: Recording the reasons for the variations
options.C: Adjusting them automatically in the Budget of the following year
options.D: Certifying them by the General Manager of the zonal railway

e: The Appropriation Accounts compare the Final Grant with actual expenditure under each head, and the reasons for the variations between the two must be recorded and explained in those accounts.

q: A clerk preparing a sector-wise summary of Government expenditure proposes to place the railway Major Heads 3001, 3002 and 5002 under General Services. These railway Major Heads are correctly grouped under the sector:

options.A: General Services
options.C: Economic Services
options.D: Grants-in-aid and Contributions

e: Railway Major Heads 3001, 3002 and 5002 relate to transport, a part of the Economic Services sector in the Government classification of expenditure, not General or Social Services.

q: Preliminary expenses incurred by a zonal railway on surveys and investigations for a proposed new railway work are treated in the accounts as:

options.A: Part of the capital cost of the work
options.B: A charge on the ordinary working expenses of the year
options.C: A debit to the Development Fund in all cases
options.D: A permanent suspense balance

e: Preliminary expenses on surveys and investigations for a proposed new work are treated as part of the capital cost of the work, being expenditure incurred in bringing the work into being.

q: The Liability Register maintained in the Accounts Office of a zonal railway serves the purpose of ensuring that:

options.A: The cash balance with the Reserve Bank is never overdrawn
options.B: The stores balances agree with the priced ledgers
options.C: The earnings of the railway agree with the Traffic Book
options.D: The commitments and liabilities incurred against a grant do not exceed the budget allotment available for the purpose

e: The Liability Register records commitments and liabilities incurred against a grant, so that the Accounts Office can ensure they do not exceed the budget allotment available for the purpose.

q: The financial powers delegated to railway officers for sanctioning expenditure, according to the nature and amount of the expenditure, are laid down in the:

options.A: Pink Book
options.C: Works Programme
options.D: Budget Register

e: The delegation of financial powers to railway officers, according to the nature and amount of expenditure, is laid down in the Schedule of Powers (SOP) of the railway.

q: Unlike the Earnings Budget, which rests on a forecast of traffic, one budget of a zonal railway is built up only after collecting the requirements of the consuming departments and the programme of works for the year, and is therefore described as a 'derived' budget. That budget is the:

options.A: Earnings Budget
options.C: Stores Budget
options.D: Capital Budget

e: The Stores Budget is a derived budget: it is built up from the requirements collected from the consuming departments and the programme of works, unlike the Earnings Budget which rests on a traffic forecast.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the gross earnings of the Railways constitute:

options.A: Tax revenue receipts
options.C: Receipts of the Public Account
options.D: Non-tax revenue receipts

e: Railway earnings are receipts of commercial departmental undertakings and are classified as non-tax revenue receipts of the Government, not tax revenue, capital receipts or Public Account receipts.

q: A deposit work is executed by the Railways for an outside party, its cost being met from the amount deposited by the party. In regard to the Works Programme (Pink Book) of the Railways, such deposit works:

options.A: Do not form part of the Works Programme, their cost being met from the deposits of the parties concerned
options.B: Are shown as itemised works in the Pink Book
options.C: Are financed out of the Development Fund
options.D: Require a separate Demand for Grant in the Budget

e: Deposit works are executed with the money deposited by the outside parties concerned, so they do not form part of the railways' own Works Programme (Pink Book) financed from railway funds.

q: The Debt Service Fund of the Railways, maintained to provide a cushion for meeting debt-service obligations in years of inadequate revenues, is credited with:

options.A: The proceeds of the bonds issued by IRFC
options.B: Appropriations made from the revenues of the Railways
options.C: The security deposits received from contractors
options.D: The fines and penalties collected by the Railways

e: The Debt Service Fund is built up by appropriations made from the revenues of the Railways, to cushion debt-service obligations in years when revenues are inadequate.

q: A minor improvement work is proposed at a station, and its cost falls within the small-value limit prescribed in the Finance Code for charging such works without treating them as capital works. A work of such small value may be charged to:

options.A: Capital
options.C: Ordinary revenue (working expenses)
options.D: Stores Suspense

e: Works of small value within the limit prescribed in the Finance Code are not treated as capital works and may be charged to ordinary revenue, i.e. the working expenses of the year.

q: A capital work of a zonal railway is financed from the Capital Fund of the Railways out of its internal resources. In the railway accounts, the work is classified under:

options.A: Major Head 3002
options.C: A separate Major Head maintained for the Capital Fund
options.D: Major Head 5002, the source of finance being indicated in the allocation of the work

e: Capital outlay is booked under Major Head 5002 whatever the source of finance; a work financed from the Capital Fund therefore stays under 5002, with the source shown in the allocation of the work.

q: The primary deficit of the Government for a year is arrived at by deducting, from the fiscal deficit of that year, the:

options.A: Revenue deficit
options.C: Interest payments
options.D: Disinvestment proceeds

e: Primary deficit is defined as fiscal deficit minus interest payments, so it is obtained by deducting the year's interest payments from the fiscal deficit.

q: A question arises as to the authority which prescribes the form in which the accounts of the Union and of the States are to be kept under Article 150 of the Constitution. That form is prescribed by:

options.A: Parliament, by law
options.B: The President, on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India himself

e: Under Article 150, the form of the accounts of the Union and the States is prescribed by the President on the advice of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Grant' from an 'Appropriation' in the Budget of the Government of India?

options.A: A grant is authorised by the Appropriation Act, while an appropriation is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand
options.B: A grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand, while the appropriation is the amount authorised by the Appropriation Act, covering both the voted grants and the charged expenditure
options.C: There is no difference between the two; the terms are interchangeable
options.D: A grant relates only to capital expenditure, while an appropriation relates only to revenue expenditure

e: A Grant is the amount voted by the Lok Sabha on a Demand for Grant, while an Appropriation is the amount authorised by the Appropriation Act, covering both the voted grants and the charged expenditure.

q: A zonal railway, while recasting its old budget statements, is directed to drop the former two-fold categorisation of Government expenditure. The distinction between 'Plan' and 'Non-Plan' expenditure in the Government Budget was discontinued with effect from the financial year:
e: The Plan and Non-Plan distinction in Government expenditure was abolished from the Budget for 2017-18, so railway budget statements were recast without that two-fold categorisation from that year.

q: In a year in which the full Budget cannot be passed before the commencement of the financial year, a 'Vote on Account' is sought from the Lok Sabha. Such a Vote on Account is normally taken to authorise expenditure for a period of about:

options.A: One month
options.C: Six months
options.D: The whole financial year

e: A Vote on Account is taken in advance of the full Budget to authorise expenditure for the initial part of the year, normally for a period of about two months.

q: During the course of a financial year, Parliament votes a supplementary grant for a service of the Railways. This supplementary grant is given legal effect, so that money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India, through:

options.A: An Appropriation Act passed for the purpose
options.B: A resolution of the Railway Board
options.C: The Finance Accounts of that year
options.D: A correction slip issued to the Finance Code

e: A supplementary grant voted by Parliament gets legal effect through an Appropriation Act, which alone authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Appropriation Bill:
1. No amendment can be proposed to the Bill which would have the effect of varying the amount of any grant already made by the Lok Sabha.
2. No amendment can be proposed to the Bill which would have the effect of altering the destination of any grant already made by the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Article 114, no amendment to an Appropriation Bill may vary the amount, or alter the destination, of any grant already made by the Lok Sabha, so both statements are correct.

q: In the classification of the railway accounts, amounts representing earnings collected but not yet deposited with, or credited by, the bank — 'Cash-in-Transit' — are classified under the:

options.A: Revenue heads
options.C: Debt heads
options.D: Remittance heads

e: Cash-in-Transit, being earnings collected but not yet credited by the bank, is a remittance transaction in course of settlement and is therefore classified under the remittance heads.

q: The Final Works Programme of a zonal railway for a financial year is finalised at the stage when:

options.A: The Budget has been approved and the budget allotment for the year has been communicated to the railway
options.B: The Budget Estimates for the year are yet to be framed by the railway
options.C: The financial year has closed and the accounts have been compiled
options.D: The Preliminary Works Programme proposals are still under preparation

e: The Final Works Programme is settled only after the Budget is passed and the year's budget allotment is communicated to the railway, fixing the outlay available for each work.

q: The lease charges payable by the Railways to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation consist of a capital component and an interest component. The interest (finance charge) component of these charges is charged to:

options.A: Capital, under the Plan Head for Leased Assets
options.C: Revenue, as part of the working expenses of the Railways
options.D: The Development Fund

e: Only the capital component of IRFC lease charges goes to capital; the interest or finance charge component is a revenue charge borne as part of the working expenses of the Railways.

q: The corpus of the Contingency Fund of India, out of which advances are made to meet unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, was enhanced in the year 2021 to:

options.A: Rs 500 crore
options.C: Rs 5,000 crore
options.D: Rs 1,00,000 crore

e: The Contingency Fund of India corpus was raised from Rs 500 crore to Rs 30,000 crore in 2021, enlarging the amount available for advances to meet unforeseen expenditure.

q: A newly posted Accounts officer needs to consult the Code volume which lays down the rules of financial management of the Railways and the delegation of financial powers. That volume is the Indian Railway Finance Code, Volume I, which mainly contains:

options.A: The rules and regulations governing the financial management of the Railways, including the delegation of financial powers
options.B: The lists of Major Heads, Minor Heads and Primary Units of classification of accounts
options.C: The rules governing the purchase and custody of stores on the Railways
options.D: The rules relating to Traffic Accounts and the compilation of the Traffic Book

e: Finance Code Volume I contains the rules of financial management of the Railways, including the delegation of financial powers; lists of heads are in Volume II and stores rules in the Stores Code.

q: An item has remained outstanding under a suspense head for a long time and is ultimately found to be irrecoverable. Such an item may be written off:

options.A: By the dealing assistant in the Accounts Office on his own authority
options.B: Only under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: Automatically at the close of the financial year, without any sanction
options.D: Only with the approval of Parliament, through a Demand for Grant

e: An irrecoverable item under a suspense head cannot be written off by the dealing staff on their own; write-off requires the sanction of the competent authority under the financial rules.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As a general rule of Government accounting, expenditure can be incurred in anticipation of a grant, at the discretion of the head of the office.
2. An advance from the Contingency Fund of India is the recognised exception through which urgent unforeseen expenditure can be met pending authorisation of the grant by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Expenditure cannot be incurred in anticipation of a grant as a matter of discretion; the recognised exception is an advance from the Contingency Fund of India for urgent unforeseen expenditure pending Parliament's authorisation, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Remittance heads of account are operated in the books of a railway primarily to record:

options.A: The earnings collected at stations during the month
options.B: The loans raised by the Railways from the market
options.C: Transactions in the course of settlement between accounting units — moneys remitted from one accounting circle to another, pending final adjustment
options.D: Expenditure incurred on the construction of new lines

e: Remittance heads record transactions in course of settlement between accounting units, such as moneys remitted from one accounting circle to another, pending their final adjustment.

q: Before the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways are taken up for voting in the Lok Sabha, they are examined in detail by:

options.A: The Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways
options.C: The Estimates Committees of the State Legislatures
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Before voting in the Lok Sabha, the Demands for Grants are examined in detail by the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways, which reports to the House.

q: A work finds a place in the Pink Book (Works Programme) of a zonal railway, and the executive proposes to start spending on it on that basis alone. The correct position is that inclusion of a work in the Pink Book:

options.A: Amounts, by itself, to sanction of the work by the Railway Board
options.B: Does not by itself amount to sanction; the work requires the sanction of the competent authority before expenditure is incurred on it
options.C: Dispenses with the preparation and sanction of estimates for the work
options.D: Authorises the executive to re-appropriate funds to the work from other heads

e: Inclusion of a work in the Pink Book is only a provision in the Works Programme; it is not itself a sanction, and expenditure can start only after the competent authority sanctions the work and its estimate.

q: Which of the following statements about re-appropriation orders is NOT correct?

options.A: Re-appropriation orders relate to a grant for a particular financial year
options.B: Such orders can be issued only up to the close of that financial year
options.C: Such orders can be issued at any time within three months after the close of the financial year
options.D: After 31 March, the unspent balance of the grant lapses

e: Re-appropriation can be ordered only during the currency of the grant, up to the close of that financial year; after 31 March the unspent balance lapses, so statement C, allowing three months beyond, is not correct.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the Consolidated Fund of India is divided into two main sections, namely:

options.A: Voted and Charged
options.C: Debt and Deposits
options.D: Plan and Non-Plan

e: In the Government accounts, the Consolidated Fund of India is divided into two main sections, the Revenue section and the Capital section.

q: The separate Railway Budget, which had been presented to Parliament since 1924-25 following the separation of railway finances, was presented for the last time for the financial year:
e: The separate Railway Budget, presented since 1924-25 after the separation of railway finances, was last presented for 2016-17; from 2017-18 it was merged with the General Budget.

q: Towards the close of a financial year, a department hurries to spend the balance of its grant in the last weeks of March so that the grant does not lapse. In the financial rules, such a rush of expenditure in the closing months of the year is regarded as:

options.A: A sign of efficient utilisation of the grant
options.C: A desirable measure to avoid the lapse of funds
options.D: A breach of financial regularity and propriety, which is to be avoided

e: A rush of expenditure in the closing months of the year to use up a grant is treated by the financial rules as a breach of financial regularity and propriety and must be avoided.

q: The Finance Bill, which gives effect to the taxation proposals of the Government for the year, is introduced in the Lok Sabha:

options.A: After the Appropriation Bill has been passed by Parliament
options.B: Along with the voting of the Demands for Grants
options.C: After the general discussion on the Budget is over
options.D: Immediately after the presentation of the Budget

e: The Finance Bill, giving effect to the year's taxation proposals, is introduced in the Lok Sabha immediately after the presentation of the Budget.

q: The Machinery and Plant (M&P) Programme of the Railways, which forms part of its annual Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes, deals with:

options.A: Procurement and replacement of machinery and plant required for workshops and the open line
options.B: Manufacture of locomotives and coaches in the production units
options.C: Purchase of stores for stocking in the stores depots
options.D: Construction of staff quarters and other welfare buildings

e: The Machinery and Plant Programme covers procurement and replacement of machinery and plant needed for workshops and the open line, as part of the annual Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes.

q: In the system of apportionment of earnings among the zonal railways, the earnings from through traffic are initially brought to account in full by:

options.A: The Railway Board, in its central books
options.B: The railway at which the traffic terminates
options.C: The office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The railway on which the traffic originates, that is, the collecting railway, and are thereafter divided among the railways concerned

e: Through traffic earnings are first brought to account in full by the originating, i.e. collecting, railway, and are thereafter apportioned among all the railways over which the traffic passed.

q: Materials which were issued to a sanctioned capital work are released from the work and returned to the stores stock. The value of such materials is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting the amount to Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways
options.C: Crediting the cost of the work concerned, thereby reducing the capital cost of that work
options.D: Treating the value as a fresh purchase of stores by the depot

e: Materials released from a work and returned to stock are credited to the cost of that work, reducing its capital cost, since the material was originally charged to the work.

q: Sub-vouchers in support of small contingent payments made by a disbursing officer of a railway are ordinarily:

options.A: Retained by the disbursing officer in his office and not forwarded to the Accounts Office
options.B: Destroyed immediately after the payment is made
options.C: Sent directly to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Published along with the monthly accounts of the railway

e: Sub-vouchers supporting small contingent payments are ordinarily retained by the disbursing officer in his own office and are not forwarded to the Accounts Office.

q: The National Investment Fund (NIF) of the Government of India, maintained in the Public Account, is credited mainly with:

options.A: The proceeds of spectrum auctions conducted by the Government
options.B: The compensation cess collected under the Goods and Services Tax
options.C: The net proceeds of the taxes shared with the States
options.D: The proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises

e: The National Investment Fund, maintained in the Public Account, is credited with the proceeds of disinvestment of Central Public Sector Enterprises.

q: A Budget note explains that a dedicated fund for road and infrastructure works draws its resources mainly from a levy on fuels. The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) is financed mainly by:

options.A: Toll collections on the national highways
options.B: A cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel
options.C: Market borrowings raised by the National Highways Authority of India
options.D: The safety surcharge levied on railway passenger fares

e: The Central Road and Infrastructure Fund is financed mainly by the cess levied on petrol and high speed diesel, set apart for road and infrastructure works.

q: In the Budget documents of the Government of India, 'Effective Capital Expenditure' represents:

options.A: Capital expenditure together with grants-in-aid given for the creation of capital assets
options.B: Capital expenditure minus the depreciation of assets during the year
options.C: Revenue expenditure and capital expenditure taken together
options.D: The fiscal deficit minus the interest payments of the year

e: Effective Capital Expenditure means capital expenditure together with grants-in-aid given to States and others for the creation of capital assets, showing the total capital-creating outlay.

q: The General Books of a zonal railway, in which the classified transactions of the railway are posted, are closed and balanced:

options.A: Every day
options.C: Once in a year, at the close of the financial year
options.D: Every month

e: The General Books, in which the classified transactions of the railway are posted, are closed and balanced every month, in step with the monthly compilation of accounts.

q: The custody of the Consolidated Fund of India and the Contingency Fund of India, and the payments into and the withdrawals from those Funds, are regulated by law made by Parliament under the Constitution in:

options.A: Article 266
options.C: Article 283
options.D: Article 292

e: Article 283 of the Constitution provides that the custody of the Consolidated and Contingency Funds and payments into and withdrawals from them are regulated by law made by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The body constituted under Article 280 of the Constitution recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
2. That body is the Finance Commission.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, which recommends the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, so both statements are correct.

q: An officer holding an imprest on a zonal railway is transferred from his post. On handing over charge, he is required to:

options.A: Account for the imprest in full and hand over the balance to his successor
options.B: Retain the imprest amount until his successor demands it from him
options.C: Deposit the imprest balance in the Public Account in his own name
options.D: Spend the unspent balance before handing over charge

e: An officer holding an imprest must, on transfer, account for it in full and hand over the unspent balance to his successor along with the charge of the post.

q: After the merger of the Railway Budget, a clerk has to exhibit the expenditure formerly covered by Demand No. 1 (Railway Board) and Demand No. 2 (Miscellaneous Expenditure) of the separate Railway Budget. These items are now accounted for under Major Head:
e: After the Budget merger, the expenditure of the former Railway Demand No. 1 (Railway Board) and No. 2 (Miscellaneous Expenditure) is accounted for under Major Head 3001, Railway Board and policy formulation.

q: A new railway line is under construction and, before it is opened for public traffic, it yields some net earnings. Such net earnings of the line under construction are:

options.A: Credited to the revenue earnings of the year
options.B: Credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of its cost
options.C: Credited to the Development Fund of the Railways
options.D: Treated as Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways

e: Net earnings yielded by a line under construction before it opens to traffic are credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of the cost of construction.

q: The Special Railway Safety Fund, set up in 2001-02 to clear the arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety assets, was created on the recommendations of:

options.A: The Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee)
options.C: The Bibek Debroy Committee
options.D: The Rakesh Mohan Committee

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund of 2001-02, meant to clear arrears of renewal of over-aged safety assets, was created on the recommendations of the Railway Safety Review Committee headed by Justice Khanna.

q: 'Ways and Means Advances' in Government finance are:

options.A: Long-term loans raised by the Government from the capital market
options.B: Grants given by the Central Government to the State Governments
options.C: Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government to tide over temporary mismatches between its receipts and its payments
options.D: Advances given by the Railways to their employees for house building

e: Ways and Means Advances are advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government to tide over temporary mismatches between its receipts and payments.

q: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, the estimates for a year are framed on the principle that:

options.A: A fixed percentage is added to the previous year's figures for every head
options.B: Only the new schemes are examined in detail, the continuing schemes being left untouched
options.C: All schemes are reviewed in detail only once in five years
options.D: Every programme or scheme has to be justified afresh, from a zero base, without reference to the level of expenditure in the past

e: Under Zero-Based Budgeting, every programme or scheme must be justified afresh from a zero base for the year, without taking the previous year's level of expenditure as given.

q: In a year in which the primary deficit of the Government is zero, it means that:

options.A: The borrowings of the Government during the year are used entirely to meet its interest payments
options.B: The Government has no outstanding debt at all
options.C: The revenue deficit of the Government for the year is also zero
options.D: The Government is not required to borrow at all during the year

e: Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments; when it is zero, the whole fiscal deficit, i.e. the year's borrowings, goes only to meet interest payments.

q: Moneys collected from the public under the small savings schemes of the Government do not form part of its revenue receipts. Such collections are credited to:

options.A: The revenue receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: The National Small Savings Fund, maintained in the Public Account of India
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The capital receipts of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Small savings collections are not Government revenue; they are credited to the National Small Savings Fund maintained in the Public Account of India, from which the depositors' claims are met.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the two broad parts into which the Budget of the Railways is divided?

options.A: The Pink Book and the Works Register
options.B: The Works Budget and the Stores Budget
options.C: The Revenue Budget, covering earnings and working expenses, and the Capital Budget, covering the annual plan outlay and its financing
options.D: The Plan Budget and the Non-Plan Budget

e: The Railway Budget has two broad parts: the Revenue Budget, covering earnings and working expenses, and the Capital Budget, covering the annual plan outlay and how it is financed.

q: Treasury Bills, through which the Government of India raises short-term funds, are issued on behalf of the Government by the:

options.A: State Bank of India
options.C: Securities and Exchange Board of India
options.D: Ministry of Finance directly, without any agency

e: Treasury Bills are issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India as its debt manager, for raising short-term funds.

q: A zonal railway has to refer to the authoritative list of Major and Minor Heads of Account (LMMH) applicable to the Central and State Governments. This list is issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
options.C: Controller General of Accounts
options.D: Railway Board

e: The List of Major and Minor Heads of Account (LMMH) for the Centre and the States is issued by the Controller General of Accounts in the Ministry of Finance.

q: Before the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) is presented to Parliament, the budget proposals of the Government are approved by the:

options.A: Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways
options.C: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Union Cabinet

e: The Budget proposals of the Government are approved by the Union Cabinet before the Annual Financial Statement is presented to Parliament.

q: A Member of Parliament wants a document that explains, clause by clause, what each provision of the Finance Bill seeks to do. The Budget document he should refer to is the:

options.A: Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill
options.C: Expenditure Profile
options.D: Detailed Demands for Grants

e: The Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill explains, clause by clause, what each provision of the Bill seeks to do, including its revenue effect.

q: A clerk preparing the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways presents the revenue expenditure estimates Sub-Major Head-wise. On the same pattern, the estimates of capital expenditure in those Demands are presented:

options.A: Minor Head-wise
options.C: Plan Head-wise
options.D: Suspense Head-wise

e: In the Demands for Grants, revenue estimates are presented Sub-Major Head-wise and, on the same pattern, capital expenditure estimates are presented Plan Head-wise.

q: The consolidated annual Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways as a whole are compiled by the Railway Board on the basis of:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets received from the stations
options.B: The Budget documents of the year
options.C: The Audit Reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The monthly Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways, production units and other accounting units

e: The Railway Board compiles the consolidated Finance Accounts of the Indian Railways from the monthly Account Currents rendered by the zonal railways, production units and other accounting units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The accounts of the Government of India, including those of the Railways, are kept broadly on the cash basis.
2. On the cash basis, a receipt is taken to account when the money is actually received, and a payment when it is actually made, rather than when the liability for it accrues.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Government accounts, including railway accounts, are kept broadly on the cash basis: a receipt is accounted when money is actually received and a payment when it is actually made, so both statements are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about the principles of Government budgeting:
1. Under the principle of annuality, the authority given by Parliament to incur expenditure holds good for one financial year only.
2. Under the principle of gross budgeting, the estimates of expenditure are framed net of the receipts expected under the same head.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Annuality means Parliament's authority to spend holds for one financial year only; but gross budgeting means estimates are framed gross, not net of receipts, so statement 2 is wrong and only statement 1 is correct.

q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is sent to the Rajya Sabha. The Rajya Sabha is required to return the Bill to the Lok Sabha, together with its recommendations, if any, within a period of:

options.A: 7 days
options.C: 30 days
options.D: 6 months

e: Under Article 109, the Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with its recommendations, if any, within 14 days of receiving it.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation form part of the internal resources of the Railways.
2. The internal resources of the Railways for financing the annual plan include the surplus (net revenue) and the amounts appropriated to the Railway Funds.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: IRFC market borrowings are extra-budgetary resources, not internal resources; internal resources comprise the surplus (net revenue) and appropriations to the Railway Funds, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the system on which the accounts of the Railways are kept from the system on which Government accounts in general are kept?

options.A: The accounts of the Railways are kept on the single-entry system, whereas Government accounts in general are kept on the double-entry system on commercial principles
options.B: Both the Railways and Government in general keep their accounts on the double-entry system on commercial principles
options.C: The accounts of the Railways are kept on commercial principles but without a Balance Sheet, whereas Government accounts in general carry a full Balance Sheet
options.D: The accounts of the Railways are kept on the double-entry system on commercial principles, whereas Government accounts in general are not so kept

e: Railway accounts are kept on the double-entry system on commercial principles, with a Balance Sheet, whereas Government accounts in general are not kept on that commercial double-entry basis.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, debit balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, representing amounts recoverable by the Railways, are shown on the liabilities side.
2. In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, credit balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, representing amounts payable by the Railways, are shown on the liabilities side.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In the Railway Balance Sheet, credit balances under debt, suspense and remittance heads, being amounts payable, appear on the liabilities side; debit balances are assets and appear on the assets side, so only statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure which results in the creation of an asset, or in the enhancement of the earning capacity of the Railways, is capital expenditure.
2. Expenditure incurred for maintaining the assets in working order and for the day-to-day operation of the Railways is revenue expenditure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Expenditure creating an asset or enhancing earning capacity is capital expenditure, while expenditure on day-to-day operation and maintaining assets in working order is revenue expenditure, so both statements are correct.

q: The revenue deficit of the Government of India for a year represents:

options.A: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts of the year
options.B: The excess of capital expenditure over capital receipts of the year
options.C: The excess of the fiscal deficit over the primary deficit of the year
options.D: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts of the year

e: Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts of the year, showing how much of the current expenditure is met from borrowings.

q: Along with the Annual Budget, the statements which the Government is required to lay before Parliament under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act include the:

options.A: Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts of the Government
options.B: Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement and the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement
options.C: Audit Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Report of the Railway Convention Committee

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Government lays before Parliament, along with the Budget, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement and the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, besides the Macro-Economic Framework Statement.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Gender Budget Statement has been presented as part of the Union Budget documents since the year 2005-06.
2. The Statement separately reflects only those schemes in which at least 50 per cent of the allocation flows to women.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The Gender Budget Statement has been part of the Union Budget since 2005-06; it covers schemes with at least 30 per cent allocation for women, not 50 per cent, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The emoluments and allowances of the President of India are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The salaries and allowances of the Judges of the Supreme Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Article 112(3), the emoluments of the President and the salaries and allowances of Supreme Court Judges are expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, so both statements are correct.

q: A clerk proposes to show the expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including the salaries and allowances of its Chairman and members, as voted expenditure in the Budget. In fact, these expenses are:

options.A: Voted by Parliament every year
options.B: Charged on the Public Account of India
options.C: Borne jointly by the Union and the States
options.D: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: The expenses of the Union Public Service Commission, including salaries of its Chairman and members, are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3) and are not voted.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pensions payable to or in respect of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.
2. The salaries and allowances of the Judges of a High Court are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: High Court Judges' pensions are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, while their salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: A zonal railway takes up a service which was not contemplated in the approved Budget, and the Accounts Office has to locate the codal provisions governing 'New Service' and 'New Instrument of Service'. In the Indian Railway Finance Code, these provisions are contained in para:
e: In the Indian Railway Finance Code, the provisions governing a New Service and a New Instrument of Service are contained in para 370.

q: Unlike the Railways, most Ministries of the Union Government got their accounts compiled departmentally, separately from audit, only after a reform. The separation of accounts from audit in the Union Government, that is, the departmentalisation of accounts, was introduced in the year:
e: Departmentalisation of Union Government accounts, separating compilation of accounts from audit, was introduced in 1976, the accounts then being compiled departmentally under the Controller General of Accounts.

q: A doubt arises in the Railway Board's office as to who advises the Government of India as its principal accounting adviser in matters of accounting. That adviser is the:

options.A: Controller General of Accounts
options.B: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Finance Secretary to the Government of India

e: The Controller General of Accounts is the principal accounting adviser to the Government of India in matters of accounting and internal audit.

q: After a Bill passed by both Houses of Parliament is presented to the President for assent, the President cannot return which of the following for the reconsideration of Parliament?

options.A: An ordinary Bill passed by both Houses
options.B: A Private Member's Bill passed by both Houses
options.C: A Money Bill
options.D: A State Bill reserved for the consideration of the President

e: The President cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration by Parliament; that power of return under Article 111 does not extend to Money Bills.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Suspense heads are final heads of account in the classification of railway accounts.
2. Balances held under suspense heads represent amounts recoverable or payable, pending their clearance to the final heads of account concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Suspense heads are not final heads; balances under them are amounts recoverable or payable held temporarily, pending clearance to the final heads of account, so only statement 2 is correct.

q: The rules relating to the forms and compilation of Government accounts are laid down in the Government Accounting Rules, 1990. These Rules were issued by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance

e: The Government Accounting Rules, 1990, laying down the form and compilation of Government accounts, were issued by the Controller General of Accounts, Ministry of Finance.

q:
At the close of a year, the working expenses of a zonal railway are compiled, including its appropriations to the various funds. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. Appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund form part of the working expenses of the Railways.
2. Such appropriations are charged to revenue under Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Appropriations from revenue to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund form part of the working expenses of the Railways and are charged under Sub-Major Head 12 of Major Head 3002, so both statements are correct.

q: The Budget Estimates of a zonal railway, before they are submitted to the Railway Board, are finally approved at the zonal level by the:

options.A: General Manager
options.B: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.C: Chief Operations Manager
options.D: Divisional Railway Manager

e: The Budget Estimates of a zonal railway are finally approved at the zonal level by the General Manager before they are submitted to the Railway Board.

q: A zonal railway has savings under one Demand for Grant and an excess under another Demand. In regard to the use of those savings, the correct position is that:

options.A: The savings can be freely utilised to meet the excess under the other Demand
options.B: The savings cannot be used to meet excess expenditure under another Demand; the excess requires regularisation by an Excess Grant for that Demand itself
options.C: The savings are transferred to the Contingency Fund of India for meeting the excess
options.D: The savings lapse automatically to the Railway Funds and meet the excess from there

e: Savings under one Demand cannot be used to meet an excess under another Demand; each Demand is a separate grant, and the excess under a Demand needs regularisation through an Excess Grant for that Demand.

q: The Union Government proposes to raise a loan on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India for financing the Railway Plan. This borrowing power of the Union is derived from Article ______ of the Constitution:
e: The Union's power to borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India is given by Article 292 of the Constitution.

q: Court deposits and similar moneys are received by a Government officer in his official capacity, otherwise than as revenues or public moneys of the Government. Under Article 284 of the Constitution, such moneys are required to be paid into the:

options.A: Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Public Account of India
options.D: Departmental account with the accredited bank

e: Under Article 284, court deposits and similar moneys received by a Government officer otherwise than as revenues or public moneys must be paid into the Public Account of India.

q:
A clerk treats the balances in the Public Account of India as the Government's own money, freely available on appropriation. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. Moneys standing in the Public Account of India belong to the Government and form part of its own revenue.
2. Disbursements out of the Public Account of India can be made only under appropriation made by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Public Account moneys are held in trust and do not belong to the Government as its revenue, and disbursements from the Public Account do not need appropriation by Parliament, so both statements are wrong.

q:
Parliament is called upon to make grants under Article 116 of the Constitution in two different situations. Consider the following statements in this connection:
1. A Vote of Credit is granted where, on account of the magnitude or the indefinite character of a service, the demand cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant.
2. An Exceptional Grant, like an ordinary grant, forms part of the services of the current financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Article 116, a Vote of Credit is granted where the magnitude or indefinite character of a service prevents details being stated; an Exceptional Grant, unlike an ordinary grant, does not form part of the current year's services, so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under suspense heads are reviewed periodically so that the items held under them are cleared by adjustment to the final heads of account as early as possible.
2. Suspense balances remaining outstanding at the close of the year are carried forward and are reflected in the Debt Head Report.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Suspense balances are reviewed periodically for early clearance to final heads, and balances still outstanding at the year end are carried forward and reflected in the Debt Head Report, so both statements are correct.

q: A difference is noticed between the balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' as per the books of a zonal railway and the balance shown in the statement of the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank. Such a difference is adjusted through the head:

options.A: Cheques and Bills
options.C: Traffic Suspense
options.D: Miscellaneous Advances

e: Differences between the railway's book balance under Deposits with Reserve Bank and the Reserve Bank Central Accounts Section statement are adjusted through the Reserve Bank Suspense head.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'internal check' from 'internal audit' in the railway accounts organisation?

options.A: Internal check is an integral part of the accounting system itself, exercised at the time the transaction is entered into and paid, whereas internal audit is a subsequent review
options.B: Internal check is carried out by the staff of the Comptroller and Auditor General, whereas internal audit is carried out by the Accounts Department
options.C: Internal check is exercised only once in five years, whereas internal audit is exercised every year
options.D: Internal check applies only to stores transactions, whereas internal audit applies to all other transactions

e: Internal check is built into the accounting system itself and operates at the time a transaction is entered into and paid, whereas internal audit is a subsequent review of transactions already passed.

q: The Cash & Pay Office of a zonal railway, which makes the bulk of the cash payments on behalf of the railway, functions as a part of the:

options.A: Commercial Department
options.C: Engineering Department
options.D: Accounts Department

e: The Cash and Pay Office, which makes the bulk of cash payments of the railway, functions as a part of the Accounts Department of the zonal railway.

q: In the Government accounts, the capital outlay of the Railways under Major Heads 5002 and 5003 has to be linked head-wise with the railway classification. For this linking, the Plan Heads of the railway classification function, under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, as the:

options.A: Sub-Major Heads
options.C: Detailed Heads
options.D: Primary Units

e: Under Major Heads 5002 and 5003, the Plan Heads of the railway classification function as the Minor Heads, linking the Government classification head-wise with the railway classification.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Works expenditure is classified under Major Heads 5002/5003 and the respective Plan Heads irrespective of whether the work is financed from Capital, the Depreciation Reserve Fund, the Development Fund, the Railway Safety Fund or the RRSK.
2. A work financed from the Development Fund is classified under Major Head 3002, as the Development Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Works expenditure is classified under Major Heads 5002/5003 by Plan Head whatever the source of finance, Capital, DRF, DF, RSF or RRSK; a DF work is therefore not booked under 3002, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: Part B of the Finance Minister's Budget Speech in Parliament deals with:

options.A: The general state of the economy
options.B: The statements laid under the FRBM Act
options.C: The taxation proposals for the ensuing year
options.D: The Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways

e: Part A of the Budget Speech covers the economy and policy, while Part B sets out the taxation proposals of the Finance Minister for the ensuing year.

q: The office in the Ministry of Finance which prepares the Union Budget, including the estimates of the Railways after the merger, is the Budget Division. This Division functions in the:

options.A: Department of Expenditure
options.C: Cabinet Secretariat
options.D: Department of Economic Affairs

e: The Budget Division, which prepares the Union Budget, functions in the Department of Economic Affairs of the Ministry of Finance.

q: The Economic Survey of India is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the guidance of the:

options.A: Finance Secretary
options.C: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog

e: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Economics Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'surrender' of funds from 're-appropriation' of funds in a grant?

options.A: Surrender means giving up savings out of a grant so that they are no longer available to the surrendering unit, whereas re-appropriation means diverting savings under one head of a grant to meet expenditure under another head of the same grant
options.B: Surrender means diverting savings from one head to another within the same grant, whereas re-appropriation means returning savings to the grant
options.C: Surrender can be made only by Parliament, whereas re-appropriation can be made only at the close of the financial year
options.D: There is no difference between the two; both terms mean the transfer of funds from one grant to another

e: Surrender is giving up savings from a grant so they cease to be available to the unit, while re-appropriation diverts savings from one head to meet expenditure under another head within the same grant.

q: Parliament votes an amount for a Demand for Grant of the Ministry of Railways, and the Railway Board then distributes that amount among the zonal railways for spending. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two stages, namely a 'Grant' and an 'Allotment'?

options.A: A grant is made by the Railway Board to the zonal railways, whereas an allotment is made by Parliament to the Ministry of Railways
options.B: A grant relates to revenue expenditure only, whereas an allotment relates to capital expenditure only
options.C: A grant is the amount voted by Parliament for a Demand for Grant, whereas an allotment is the distribution of that grant by the Railway Board among the zonal railways and other units for incurring expenditure
options.D: A grant is valid for three years, whereas an allotment is valid for one year only

e: A Grant is the amount voted by Parliament on a Demand for Grant; an Allotment is the distribution of that grant by the Railway Board among the zonal railways and other units for spending it.

q: A clerk uses the words 'Capital' and 'Capital Fund' interchangeably in a note on railway finance. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two?

options.A: 'Capital' denotes the amounts of the Capital Fund invested in works, whereas the 'Capital Fund' denotes budgetary support from the General Finances
options.B: There is no difference between the two; the terms are interchangeable
options.C: 'Capital' is a source of revenue receipts, whereas the 'Capital Fund' is a part of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: 'Capital' denotes the capital provided to the Railways by the General Finances (Gross Budgetary Support), whereas the 'Capital Fund' is a fund created out of the Railways' own internal resources, principally the surplus, for financing capital works

e: Capital is the capital provided by General Finances as Gross Budgetary Support, while the Capital Fund is a railway fund built from the Railways' own internal resources, mainly the surplus, for financing capital works.

q: Two safety funds of the Railways, the Railway Safety Fund and the Special Railway Safety Fund, are sometimes confused with each other. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two?

options.A: The Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund with a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and used for works relating to level crossings and road over/under bridges, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund with a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore set up in 2001-02 to wipe out the arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety assets
options.C: Both the funds are continuing funds credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund is financed entirely by Gross Budgetary Support, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares

e: The Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund fed by the safety surcharge on passenger fares for level crossing and road over/under bridge works, while the SRSF was a one-time Rs 17,000 crore fund of 2001-02 for clearing renewal arrears.

q: Two registers are maintained in the Accounts Office of a zonal railway in connection with works expenditure and the commitments against grants. Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Works Register from the Liability Register?

options.A: The Works Register records, work-wise, the sanctions, budget allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work, whereas the Liability Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, against which payments have yet to be made
options.B: The Works Register records the commitments incurred against a grant, whereas the Liability Register records the progressive expenditure on each work
options.C: Both registers record the sanctions, allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work
options.D: The Works Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Liability Register is maintained in the Accounts Office

e: The Works Register records work-wise sanctions, allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work, while the Liability Register records commitments such as orders and contracts placed, against which payment is yet to be made.
